headline: Ward 39 ranks 12th of 50, strong on governance, weak on school funding and nightlife.
summary:
Ward 39 covers North Park, Forest Glen, Albany Park, and Irving Park on the city's Northwest Side. It ranks 12th out of 50 wards overall, solidly in the top third of Chicago, with its clearest strengths in civic measures. The ward has the second-most libraries in the city and one of the widest ranges of religious traditions among its houses of worship. Building permits here also move faster than in most of Chicago, and the ward spends a larger-than-typical share of its aldermanic menu money on parks.

The weak points sit in schools and in the kind of places that bring people together outside their own block. Per-pupil school spending ranks last of all 50 wards. Licensed music and dance venues are among the scarcest in the city, and a modeled estimate puts the share of residents seeing friends weekly well below most other wards. Over half the ward's park water fountains also carry a history of elevated lead readings, more than in almost every other ward. Together, the numbers describe a ward that's steady on the basics of city government but thin on nightlife and casual social contact.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers need a second look. Alder attendance for the current council session ranks third out of 50, which sounds strong, but Chicago redrew ward boundaries in 2023, so the figure reflects today's Ward 39 rather than one continuous seat across the full session, and the source itself rates the underlying data only medium confidence. Park spending from the aldermanic menu fund also ranks third, but the caveat here is different. The middle half of all 50 wards sit within zero points of each other on this measure, so nearly the whole city is bunched together, and a small dollar shift can move a ward several spots. The weaker rankings carry their own caveats too. The estimate that only 16.6 percent of residents see friends weekly comes from a model built on national survey data and the ward's demographics rather than any direct count, and the source rates it low confidence.

news.headline: Art Institute's 'Project Windows' Gets Boost From NW Side Businesses
news.note: Six spots across the ward, including Superdawg and the Edgebrook branch library, are displaying local artwork this summer as part of the Art Institute's annual Project Windows program.

news.headline: Police SWAT Team Officer, Woman Shot In Albany Park: 'Absolutely Tragic'
news.note: A police SWAT officer and a 67-year-old woman were shot during a domestic incident and hostage situation in Albany Park, and a suspect was later taken into custody.

news.headline: Protesters Want ICE Out After Chaotic Albany Park Arrest: 'Midway Blitz Is Over, But ICE Has Not Left'
news.note: About 150 people rallied in Horner Park after federal immigration agents made a chaotic arrest at Lawrence and Kedzie in Albany Park.
